% Proof attached by reference, not adjacency. Edge cases showcased:
%   - a proof whose \begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{...}] names its target
%   - an unrelated statement sitting between the theorem and its proof
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath, amsthm, amssymb}

\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}

\begin{document}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:key}
The square of any odd integer is odd.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:filler}
This lemma sits between the theorem and its proof to prevent adjacency matching.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:key}]
Write the odd integer as $2k + 1$; its square is $4k^2 + 4k + 1$, which is odd.
\end{proof}

\end{document}
